chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ali al-Qurashi from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. Umar from Yunus b. Thibyan from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:

While Musa b. Imran (peace be upon him) was speaking to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, he saw a man beneath the shade of the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So he said: O my Lord, who is this whom Your Throne shades? So He said: This one was good to his parents and did not spread gossip.

key_terms.النَّمِيمَةِ: Gossip/tale-bearing -- spreading rumors that sow discord between people
key_terms.بَارًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ: Good to his parents -- filial piety, a paramount virtue in Islam
key_terms.عَرْشِ اللَّهِ: The Throne of Allah -- the greatest of all created things in Islamic cosmology

ai.seo_question: What two qualities earn the shade of Allah's Throne according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes a scene where Prophet Musa (AS), during his intimate conversation with God, sees a man being honored under the shade of Allah's Throne. When Musa asks about this person's identity, Allah reveals that the man earned this distinction through two qualities: filial piety (birr al-walidayn) and abstaining from gossip (namimah). In early Islamic society, these two traits were considered fundamental to social harmony -- one preserving family bonds, the other preserving community trust.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him
